items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: The interviewee mentions 'Paul Detroit' only in the context of his brother's name ('One was named John and one was named Paul') and later refers to 'Paul Detroit' as the person who wrote an obituary about his brother ('he says that Paul Detroit played in the Orphian Pitman with his brother Johnny's

ctx.x: All right. Why don't you name your name? Yeah. I'd like to get your full name down.

My name is John G-O-H-N, capital D-E, capital D-R-O-I-T, Good Rock. And the middle name? No middle name. In my family there were two uncles who had money. One was named John and one was named Paul. And in the whole family you find nothing but John and Paul. That's what you call a coincidence.
You call that ignorance. They used to speak French so I couldn't understand them.

items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] And he's Dutch's brother? >> [INTERVIEWEE] Dutch's brother.

ctx.x: Dutch's brother. You know, it would take the whole book to tell my story. I know. But I made a terrible mistake. Now understand that I respected Dr. Sushaw and he was my friend. I played for his daughter's supper dance when she was queen of the carnival. I knew his wife when she was a young girl, Mari Estupa, her name was. And he was publishing the second line and I was a member of the jazz club. And I tend to join again. I have the application. But I'm waiting until January. Why give him $10 for December?…
I want you to ask you something. Are you sure? Yeah, sure.
